issuing_body: Optum State Government Solutions for Minnesota Department of Human Services
title: Minnesota Payment Integrity: Phase 1 Summary Report – Achievements, Findings and Recommendations

money.notes: Report defines these as funds that can be recouped based on identified issues/policy violations. Do not assume the full amount was already collected in cash.
Report says these may reflect missing/vague policy vulnerabilities and may require medical-necessity record review. Not a fraud-loss or cash-recovery figure.
Report describes decline in inappropriate billing from Q3 to Q4 2025 and defines cost avoidance as preventing future expense, not reducing current spending.
Paid-claim high-risk service-area provider findings reported to the State for review as of 2026-01-13.
Pre-pay warrant-cycle analytic findings reported to the State for review as of 2026-01-15.

supports: The report evaluated 14 named high-risk service/program areas using fee-for-service paid-claims data; managed-care claims were outside scope.
The report's service list includes HSS, Peer Recovery, EIDBI, ICS, NEMT, ARMHS, PCA/CFSS, Adult Day, Recuperative Care, IHS, Adult Companion, Night Supervision, ACT and IRTS.
does_not_support: The >$1.7B potential-recovery figure is not proven fraud, stolen money, restitution, or cash recovered.
The >$52.3M source term 'direct recoveries' should not be rendered as cash collected unless DHS separately documents collection; the report itself defines it as funds that can be recouped.
Managed-care claims were not part of the Phase 1 data scope, so the report is not a complete statewide Medicaid-claims measurement.
The 14 high-risk categories are not 14 criminal case families.
